subject: DONE s365: PPI mis-lexes an anon sub's ATTRIBUTE at expression start as a LABEL (op/sub_lval.t de-gated)
description:
TWO layers, both fixed s365:

1. `Structure::For` re-bless (Pl/Parser2.pm, _lower_compound): a `for`/`foreach`
   whose parens PPI lexed as PPI::Structure::For is re-blessed to
   PPI::Structure::List when there is a loop VARIABLE or no `;` separator —
   the discriminator is that a C-style `for` never has a loop variable before
   its parens.  Removes the "Parser2 TODO: C-style for with continue block"
   die.

2. THE REAL CAUSE — a PPI 1.291 LEXER BUG (registered docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md
   §7): at the START of an expression `sub :lvalue { … }` tokenizes as
   Label('sub :') + Word('lvalue'), chained attributes chain as more Labels,
   and inside a `for` list each label even gets a STATEMENT of its own.
   Mid-expression the same text tokenizes correctly, which is why
   `my $f = sub :lvalue {…}` always worked.  Nothing downstream saw an anon
   sub → "Missing case: [" → the whole statement was replaced by a PARSE ERROR
   comment (silent code drop).
   Fix: Pl::Parser2::_normalize_anon_sub_attrs (document-level, beside the
   other PPI repairs) merges the split statements, drops the attribute run
   (incl. `:prototype($$)`'s own parens), re-blesses Label→Word('sub').
   Plus Pl/PExpr.pm's existing "strip prototype after sub" pass in
   handle_subcalls generalised to also consume (':' Attribute) pairs — that is
   the CORRECTLY-lexed mid-expression spelling, which also had no handler.

VERIFIED: op/sub_lval.t 12/58 = its perl-suite-run.tsv snapshot C_ok (bar met;
residue is `undef-fn:main::pl-rlv1t`, a different axis).  Gate-set over both
audit populations 23 → 22 gated files, zero new gates.  Guard rows in
Pl/t/transpile-test-09.t incl. inverse guards (a REAL loop label still lowers
as a label; attribute-free anon subs untouched).
